title: Chapter 23: The Malevolent 1
content:
Chapter 23

Right on cue, the unconscious Jin Ling sat straight up.

With both elders watching, the boy stumbled to his feet with his eyes still clamped shut, sleepwalking across the pavers. Curious to see where this trance was leading, Wei Wuxian held back and didn't make a move. Jin Ling edged slowly around him, stepped one leg out, and planted himself right back inside the breached wall—standing squarely inside the cavity where he’d just been unearthed. He dropped his hands flat against his sides, settling into the exact stiff, upright posture he’d been found in.

Wei Wuxian dragged him right back out of the dirt, caught between laughter and a creeping chill. He was just about to tell Lan Wangji that hanging around here was a terrible idea when an enraged wave of barking tore through the woods, making him jump half out of his skin. Ever since they’d stepped through the breach, the black-maned hound had stayed glued to the opening, wagging its tail while waiting with anxious, pleading patience for them to carry its master back out, quiet as a mouse.

Yet right now, it was snarling with twice the ferocity it had shown all night.

Lan Wangji’s voice went low. "Trouble outside."

He reached out to help the boy, but Wei Wuxian hoisted Jin Ling onto his back first. "Let's check it out!"

They retraced their steps at a sprint. Ducking out into the open air, they spotted the hound facing away into the trees, its throat vibrating with a low, venomous growl. Wei Wuxian had forced himself to tough it out this far, but that gutter rattle was his personal kryptonite; he instinctively backpedaled three paces. Naturally, the hound whipped around, caught sight of its master slung over the lunatic's shoulders, and came bounding straight at him!

Wei Wuxian let out a strangled shriek, seconds away from tossing Jin Ling like a hot potato, when Lan Wangji smoothly slid into the line of fire.

The hound skidded to a dead halt, tucking its tail firmly between its legs once more. The reason it wasn't panting was that its jaws were clamped around something. Lan Wangji stepped forward, bent down, and plucked a scrap of torn cloth from between its fangs before bringing it over for Wei Wuxian to inspect.

It looked like the hem of a robe.

Someone had been creeping around out here, spying on the fortress—and whatever they were up to was plainly suspicious, or the hound's barking wouldn't be dripping with this much raw aggression.

"They can't have gotten far," Wei Wuxian said. "After them!"

"No need," Lan Wangji replied. "I know who it is."

"So do I," Wei Wuxian agreed. "The rumors on Xinglu Ridge, the walking corpses, the labyrinth, the fortress—they're all tied to the same outfit. Same with those sabres. But if we don't catch the culprit red-handed right now, cornering them later is going to be a massive headache."

Lan Wangji glanced at him. "I will pursue. You and Jin Ling?"

"I'll carry him down the ridge and find a place to lay low in Qinghe," Wei Wuxian said, rattling off the plan. "Right back where we bumped into that street vendor earlier. We'll rendezvous there."

The exchange was clipped and hurried. Lan Wangji hesitated for a single breath, prompting Wei Wuxian to urge, "Go, before they vanish completely! I'll be there, I swear!"

At that soft promise—I'll be there—Lan Wangji looked him deep in the eyes. Without another word, he turned on his heel to give chase.

The hound immediately bounded forward to follow Jin Ling, sending Wei Wuxian into an absolute panic: "Wait, wait, wait! Take the dog with you! Take the damn dog!!!"

Lan Wangji was forced to pivot back, leveling a cool, commanding glare down at the beast. Duly intimidated, the hound whined pathetically and fell into step behind the white robes, matching Lan Wangji's pace into the woods while glancing back over its shoulder at Jin Ling every few steps.

Wei Wuxian wiped the cold sweat from his brow. Casting one last look at the cluster of pale, tomb-like fortresses, he adjusted Jin Ling's weight across his back and made a beeline down Xinglu Ridge.

Dusk was settling over the mountains. Lugging an unconscious teenager while caked in mud and grime naturally drew curious stares from every passerby on the road. Arriving back on the busy strip where Jin Ling had sicced his dog earlier that afternoon, Wei Wuxian ducked into an inn. Using the coin pouch he’d lifted from Lan Wangji, he bought two fresh sets of robes, booked a private room, and set to work.

He stripped off the boy's muddied, wrinkled peony-crested over-robe, tugged off his riding boots, and was just about to peel off the rest when his hands froze.

Along Jin Ling’s calf sat an odd, dark patch.

Wei Wuxian dropped into a crouch and rolled the trouser leg up. It wasn't a shadow. It was a mottled, bruised black stain—and definitely not from a physical strike.

It was a Malignant Curse Mark.

Curse marks were spiritual brands left by dark entities upon their prey. Once branded, it meant the victim had crossed paths with something deeply, violently unholy. A marker was an open invoice; the monster was guaranteed to return for collection. Maybe months down the line, maybe before dawn. At best, it claimed the limb bearing the mark; at worst, it simply took your life.

Jin Ling’s entire lower leg had turned an inky, purplish black, the discoloration visibly creeping upward. Wei Wuxian had never seen a curse mark this densely concentrated or spreading this fast. His face tightened. Lowering the trouser hem, he unfastened the boy's inner tunic; seeing the chest and abdomen pristine, free from the dark rot, he finally let out the breath he’d been holding.

Right then, Jin Ling’s eyelashes fluttered, and his eyes snapped open.

He blinked stupidly at the ceiling for a second before the chilly draft against his bare skin jolted him awake. Scrambling backward in a panic, his cheeks flushed scarlet as he sputtered, "W-w-what the hell are you doing?!"

Wei Wuxian gave an easy chuckle. "Oh, look who's awake."

Jin Ling looked like he’d just woken up inside a nightmare. Clamping his open shirt shut, he plastered his back against the headboard. "What are you trying to pull?! Where are my clothes?! Where’s my sword?! Where’s my dog?!"

"I'm putting clothes on you right now, aren't I?" Wei Wuxian drawled, adopting the soft, patient tone of an elderly grandmother fussing over a beloved toddler.

Disheveled, hair sticking up in every direction, Jin Ling pressed harder against the plaster wall. "I'm not a cutsleeve!!!"

Wei Wuxian beamed with pure delight. "What a coincidence—I am!"

Jin Ling lunged for the sword leaning against the bedpost, looking thoroughly prepared to run the lunatic through before taking his own life to defend his honor.

Wei Wuxian could barely hold his laughter in, clutching his stomach as he snorted, "What are you sweating for? It’s a joke! I nearly broke my back digging you out of that wall, and you can't even toss out a simple thank-you?"

Jin Ling took a frantic second to rake a hand through his birds-nest hair, trying to salvage a shred of dignity. "If—if it weren't for that, the second you laid a hand on my clothes, I would've slaughtered you ten thousand times over!"

"Easy there," Wei Wuxian said, waving a placating hand. "Dying once was painful enough, thanks. Come on, put the steel away."

Still in a daze, Jin Ling actually listened, letting the blade drop.

During the spiritual interrogation earlier, his living soul had been drifting, leaving his memories hazy at best; yet in the back of his mind, he had a vague awareness that this ridiculous man was the one who had shoveled him out of the mud and carried him down the mountain. Trapped in that suffocating dark, he’d spent hours fully conscious, drowning in a despair so absolute he thought he was done for. To think the person who broke through the bricks—shattering that suffocating terror—was the very lunatic he’d despised at first sight.

His face shifted through shades of white and crimson, dizzy, embarrassed, his thoughts drifting without an anchor.

Catching the evening gloom settling outside the window and the faint twinkle of early stars, Jin Ling’s eyes went wide. While Wei Wuxian bent down to gather the clean robes from the floorboards, Jin Ling vaulted off the mattress, kicked his boots on, snatched his muddy over-robe, and bolted straight out the door.

Wei Wuxian had assumed the kid would be laid out for hours after taking that kind of punishment; turns out youth really was boundless, bouncing back like a wild colt in the blink of an eye. Remembering the toxic curse mark eating its way up the boy's leg, he shouted after him, "What are you running for?! Get back here!"

Jin Ling hauled the wrinkled, dirt-caked robe over his shoulders as he sprinted down the hall, yelling back, "Don't you dare follow me!"

Tall, long-legged, and surprisingly nimble, he cleared the stairs in two bounds and blew past the inn's front threshold. Wei Wuxian chased him through three different intersections before losing the trail entirely in the falling dusk.

Combing through the alleys as the streets emptied out, Wei Wuxian gritted his teeth in sheer frustration.Unbelievable. This kid is completely, utterly impossible!

Just as he was about to throw in the towel, an irritated, sharp baritone cut through the quiet lane ahead: "A few harsh words and you go vanishing into thin air? Who do you think you are, some pampered young mistress? Your temper gets worse every damn day!"

Jiang Cheng!

Wei Wuxian ducked into the nearest shadow on reflex.

Jin Ling’s defensive whine fired right back: "I came back in one piece, didn't I?! Stop nagging me!"

So the boy hadn't come to Qinghe alone. Naturally—Jiang Cheng had personally patrolled Dafan Mountain to back him up, so why would he skip out on this hunt? From the sound of it, the uncle and nephew had gotten into a screaming match down in town, prompting Jin Ling to stomp off to Xinglu Ridge on his own. The boy’s manic rush to escape the inn made sense now: Jiang Cheng had likely threatened to skin him alive if he wasn't back before sundown.

"One piece?" Jiang Cheng snapped. "You look like you've been dragged through a sewer ditch and you call that 'one piece'?! Have some shame wearing your clan's crest in that state—get back to your room and change this instant! Now spill: what did you run into up there?"

Jin Ling huffed, voice dripping with irritation. "I told you, nothing! I took a spill, that's all. Complete waste of time. Ow!" he yelled. "Stop dragging my collar! I'm not three years old!"

"Clearly I haven't disciplined you enough!" Jiang Cheng barked. "I don't care if you're thirty, I'll drag you whenever I please. Sneak off on your own without reporting again, and you're getting the whip!"

"I went alone because I don't need anyone's charity and I don't need a babysitter!"

Listening from the dark, Wei Wuxian couldn't help agreeing:Say what you will, Jiang Cheng wasn't lying about that pampered young mistress temper.

Jiang Cheng scoffed, "And where did that get you? What did you catch? Where's that spiritual hound your little uncle gifted you?"

Chased off to god-knows-where by Lan Zhan,Wei Wuxian mused.

Right as the thought crossed his mind, two sharp, painfully familiar barks echoed from the mouth of the alley.

Wei Wuxian went instantly rigid. His legs moved entirely on autopilot, launching him out of the shadows like an arrow with a fire lit under its tail. The black-maned hound came bounding in from the opposite end of the lane, darting right past Wei Wuxian to plant its front paws against Jin Ling's boots, tail whipping happily against the boy's shins.

The hound's arrival meant Lan Wangji had likely bagged the prowler by the fortress and was already waiting at their rendezvous spot. Unfortunately, Wei Wuxian didn't have the luxury to dwell on logistics.

His blind sprint had dumped him straight into the open—right in front of Jiang Cheng, Jin Ling, and a whole squad of Yunmeng Jiang cultivators.

The alley froze for a single, breathless second. Wei Wuxian slowly turned on his heel to casually stroll away.

He barely managed three strides before the sharp hiss of crackling lightning tore through the air. A whip of spitting violet current lashed out like a venomous viper, coiling tight around his shins. A searing, numbing jolt ripped up his spine, yanking his legs clean out from under him as he hit the pavers with a solid thud. Before he could roll, fingers twisted into his back collar, hoisting him effortlessly off the ground.

Wei Wuxian’s hand shot toward his Spirit-Locking Pouch, but a quicker hand swatted it away, snatching the relic from his grip.

Hauling him along like a sack of grain, Jiang Cheng strode up to the nearest storefront and booted open the half-shuttered timber door.

The shopkeeper was just wrapping up for the night when a strikingly handsome, richly dressed cultivator kicked his front door in, carrying a captive by the scruff like an executioner ready to gut a pig right on the floorboards. Terrified out of his wits, the man froze behind the counter. A Jiang disciple stepped forward, muttered a few quiet instructions, and shoved a hefty pouch of silver into the shopkeeper's trembling hands; the old man scurried into the back rooms without looking back. Without needing orders, the rest of the disciples fanned out, sealing the building tight from rafters to foundation.

Jin Ling lingered near the doorway, hovering in tense, uncertain silence.

Jiang Cheng shot him a lethal glare. "I'll deal with you in a minute. Plant your feet right there and don't move!"

In all his sixteen years, Jin Ling had never seen that look on his uncle's face.

The man who had shouldered the Yunmeng Jiang Clan from a young age was perpetually severe, bitter, and cold—never sparing kind words, never showing mercy. Yet right now, though Jiang Cheng was fighting with every fiber of his being to keep his features locked down, his eyes were burning with a terrifying, feverish intensity.

That face, normally wrapped in layers of haughty cynicism and dark storm clouds, had suddenly snapped into sharp, vivid focus. Looking at him, it was impossible to tell whether he was grinding his teeth in bone-deep hatred—or trembling on the edge of wild, frantic ecstasy.
